clue.text: Infernally complicated "eddy" clue

indicators.note: complicated tells us the letters of the quoted words are tangled into another order

explanation.surface: A setter boasts of a fiendishly tricky clue built round the word eddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' signals the anagram of EDDY CLUE; the quotation marks just make the fodder look like a specimen word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild old oaths meaning devilishly or confoundedly, deuce being a euphemism for the devil.

clue.text: For a prophetess, contrariwise, difficult to be without honour

indicators.note: contrariwise means the whole assembly is read the other way round
without here means outside, so the honour sits within the word for difficult

parts.note: difficult means hard
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: For a seer, being without any honour is hard, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking; it means outside. HAROBED read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Judges she is the prophet and judge who leads Israel with Barak.

clue.text: Complaint — rut needs repair, one above Heraclitus's home

indicators.note: in a down clue above puts the numeral on top of the region
needs repair means the word rut must be rebuilt in another order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
the poet Heraclitus, friend of Callimachus, came from Halicarnassus in Caria in Asia Minor

explanation.surface: A grumble about a rutted road, with a Greek philosopher's homeland thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' is an illness. The Heraclitus meant is the poet of Halicarnassus, mourned in Cory's 'They told me, Heraclitus', not the philosopher of Ephesus.
explanation.definitionFit: Nettle rash or hives is a skin ailment, and an ailment can be called a complaint.

clue.text: A sort of general increase

indicators.note: a sort of means a rearranged version of the following word

explanation.surface: A broad, general rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sort of' signals the anagram of GENERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something bigger is to increase it.

clue.text: Little girls reading stories about a ship

indicators.note: about means the stories go round the other letters

parts.note: stories can be lies
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: Young girls reading tales about a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reading' is only a joining word in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots lasses with the diminutive ending are young girls.

clue.text: Cite Benito, after notice

indicators.note: after puts the dictator's title behind the notice in the answer

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper
Benito Mussolini was styled Il Duce, the leader

explanation.surface: An instruction to quote Mussolini once a notice has been given.
explanation.definitionFit: To adduce evidence is to bring it forward or quote it as proof.

clue.text: Valuation by academician is seen in dismay

indicators.note: seen in means these letters appear inside the word for dismay

parts.note: to appal is to dismay
RA stands for Royal Academician

explanation.surface: An academy member's assessment greeted with horror.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal is an assessment of worth.

clue.text: Uncommonly glad to receive one here in Ireland

indicators.note: to receive means the jumbled letters take the word one inside them
uncommonly means in an unusual way, so the word glad is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is unusually happy to welcome a visitor to Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncommonly' turns GLAD into DGAL, which takes in ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A county in the far north-west of the Irish Republic is a place in Ireland.

clue.text: This bit of verse a minor blow for Pierre?

parts.note: coup is French for a blow, Pierre standing for a Frenchman
-let is a suffix making something smaller, as in booklet

explanation.surface: A Frenchman suffers a slight knock.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together the pieces suggest a French 'little blow'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of rhyming lines is a short piece of poetry.

clue.text: Potemkin for instance in Ben's joint

parts.note: Ben Battle is the legless soldier in Thomas Hood's comic ballad Faithful Nelly Gray, so Ben's gives his surname plus S
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A mention of the famous mutinous Russian ship turning up in some Ben's bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like a pub or bar; it is the body part. Hood's Ben Battle lost his legs in battle, a joke on hips.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potemkin was a Russian warship of the heavy armoured class, famous for its 1905 mutiny.

clue.text: Joshua's father takes in nothing of this part of speech

indicators.note: takes in means the father's name swallows the zero inside itself

parts.note: in the Bible Joshua is the son of Nun
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A biblical father absorbing nothing of a grammatical category.
explanation.definitionFit: A naming word is one of the classical parts of speech, alongside verb and adjective.

clue.text: Abou Ben Adhem's nocturnal visitor has us all taped?

definitions.text: Abou Ben Adhem's nocturnal visitor has us all taped?

parts.words: Abou Ben Adhem's nocturnal visitor has us all taped?
parts.note: in Leigh Hunt's poem Abou Ben Adhem wakes to find an angel writing names in a book of gold; to have us all taped is both to have us sized up and to have our deeds on tape

explanation.surface: The angel who visited the poem's hero by night knows all about us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taped' is slang for summed up, but also hints at a tape recording of our deeds.
explanation.definitionFit: In tradition a heavenly scribe notes down every person's good and bad deeds for judgement day.

clue.text: "At least we'll die with — on our back" (Macbeth)

definitions.text: "At least we'll die with — on our back" (Macbeth)

parts.words: "At least we'll die with — on our back" (Macbeth)
parts.note: Macbeth's last defiant line in Act 5 calls for the armour to be worn as he dies; the missing word fills the gap

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from Macbeth's final battle speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Here the word is the old term for a knight's armour, the gear a fighting man is strapped into.

clue.text: Old Jewish council and shrine, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps means these letters might be arranged into another order

explanation.surface: An ancient Jewish assembly and a holy place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals the anagram of AND SHRINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The supreme court and council of elders in ancient Jerusalem.

clue.text: Is love dead, or just set apart?

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, so the letter O
the late person is one who has died

explanation.surface: A lovelorn question: has romance died, or are we merely separated?
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' and 'dead' read as a romance ending; they are tennis zero and the late.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate something is to cut it off and keep it separate from others.

clue.text: Cattle-caller's crafty plan to capture wild heron

definitions.note: the possessive here stands for has, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: to capture means the first jumble takes the second inside it
crafty means the word plan is cunningly rearranged
wild means the word heron is scrambled

explanation.surface: A herdsman's cunning scheme to catch a wild bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crafty' makes ALPN from PLAN, and 'wild' makes ENHOR from HERON, which goes in before the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiss herdsmen blow this long wooden instrument to call cows down from the mountain pasture.

clue.text: A card about the pitcher

explanation.surface: A playing card that turns up near a baseball pitcher.
explanation.walkthrough: A baseball pitcher stands at the centre of the infield, so this shape lies all about him.
explanation.definitionFit: One is a card of the red suit with lozenge pips; the other is the square baseball infield surrounding the pitcher's mound.

clue.text: One cast out from the devilish maelstrom

indicators.note: from the means the letters are taken out of the run of the next words

explanation.surface: Someone thrown out of a hellish whirlpool.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'devILISH MAELstrom'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Abraham's son by Hagar was driven out, so the name means an outcast.

clue.text: Matriarchal head of Chinese dynasty appears in dumb show

parts.note: a matriarch heads the family, mother or mum
the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644

explanation.surface: An empress dowager appears in a silent play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' looks like a first-letter instruction, but the whole phrase gives MUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Mummers' plays are traditional performances, and a silent mimed show is called mummery.

clue.text: Tom's tongue, one of those proverbially fast movers

definitions.text: one of those proverbially fast movers

explanation.surface: Someone called Tom talks very fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Great Tom is the big bell at Christ Church, Oxford, and the striker inside a bell is its tongue; British 'like the clappers' means very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell's hanging striker is called its tongue, and the British idiom says anything quick goes like these strikers.

clue.text: The frankness of a scandalous theatrical wife

explanation.surface: The candour of a gossipy stage wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Candour is the malicious gossip in Sheridan's comedy The School for Scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankness is honesty in speaking, and Sheridan's character Mrs Candour spreads scandal.

clue.text: Historically to outlaw a race isn't common

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race
ain't is a common, nonstandard form of isn't

explanation.surface: Banning a contest was once unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'common' means vulgar speech, not frequent.
explanation.definitionFit: In old law, attainder stripped a condemned person of civil rights, effectively making them an outlaw.

clue.text: Alter look of cathedral city erected after the others

indicators.note: after puts the upturned city behind the others in the answer

parts.note: the rest means the others

indicators.note: erected in a down clue means the city is written upwards

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Changing a cathedral city's appearance once everything else has been built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns ELY into YLE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a new style is to change its appearance.

clue.text: Smith using these to fight so furiously?

definitions.text: Smith using these to fight so furiously?

parts.words: Smith using these to fight so furiously?
parts.note: a blacksmith's working tools give the idiom for fighting with great vigour

explanation.surface: A blacksmith wielding his tools as weapons in a fierce brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith beats metal with his striking tool and holds it with gripping tools, and the phrase also means with great energy.

clue.text: Oriental garb — Cleopatra's: attendant returned

indicators.note: returned means the attendant's name is read back to front

parts.note: Iras is one of Cleopatra's waiting women in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra

explanation.surface: Cleopatra's servant comes back wearing Eastern dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A long wrapped garment worn by women in India and elsewhere in South Asia.

clue.text: Store of eg goods or poetry is destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed means the words are broken up and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A lament that a stock of goods or verse has been wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' signals the anagram of OR POETRY IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A depository or warehouse is a place where goods are kept.

clue.text: Standard number returned to the vessel

parts.note: a standard is a flag

indicators.note: returned means the abbreviation for number is read backwards

explanation.surface: A regimental flag and its number are sent back to the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns NO into ON. 'vessel' suggests a ship; it is a drinking jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A large jug or bottle for wine or ale is a vessel for liquids.

clue.text: Coppers come round about initiation of the false claim

indicators.note: come round means the coins enclose the other letters

parts.note: pence are copper coins
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: initiation of means the opening letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Police officers gather round to investigate the start of a bogus claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police; they are pennies. RE and T go inside PENCE after its P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence is a false show or claim made to deceive.
